name: Ahab
description: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy

points: Ahab son of Omri reigns twenty-two years in Samaria and does evil above all that were before him.

note.label: 1 Kings 16: Baasha to Ahab and the Rise of Baal Worship

points: Elijah the Tishbite, of the inhabitants of Gilead, said unto Ahab that as the Lord God of Israel liveth, before whom he stands, there shall not be dew nor rain these years but according to his word. Elijah prayed and it was no rain.

note.label: 1 Kings 17: The Word of the Lord in Elijah's Mouth Is Truth

points: After many days the word of the Lord came to Elijah in the third year: Go show thyself unto Ahab, and I will send rain upon the earth. There was a sore famine in Samaria.

note.label: 1 Kings 18: The Lord, He Is the God

points: The famine was so sore it was hitting the animals, so Ahab and Obadiah divided the land between them, each going his own way to seek fountains and brooks to find grass to save the horses and mules alive. This was the fruit of the drought Elijah had pronounced.

note.label: 1 Kings 18: The Lord, He Is the God

points: Obadiah was afraid, for Ahab had searched every nation and kingdom to find and slay Elijah; that is how badly Jezebel wanted him dead, so she got Ahab to do her bidding. This is why Elijah had been on the run, first by Jordan, then years with the widow.

Obadiah feared that the spirit of the Lord would carry Elijah away and Ahab would slay him for a false report, so he pleaded his own record: he feared the Lord from his youth and had hidden a hundred of the Lord's prophets by fifty in a cave. Elijah swore by the Lord of hosts that he would surely show himself to Ahab that day, and so Obadiah went to Ahab, and Ahab came to meet Elijah.

note.label: 1 Kings 18: The Lord, He Is the God

points: Art thou he that troubleth Israel? Now he's trying to shift the blame. He's trying to blame the messenger for the consequences of their own disobedience, for Ahab's own disobedience.

note.label: The Inevitability of Obsolescence & Agony of Defeat

points: When Ahab saw Elijah he said, Art thou he that troubleth Israel? That is the mind of a wicked person: he blamed the trouble on the ordained prophet of God rather than on his own wickedness. When the spirit is gone, wisdom cannot enter a malicious soul, so Ahab had thoughts without understanding.

note.label: 1 Kings 18: The Lord, He Is the God

points: Elijah told Ahab to get up and eat and drink, for there was a sound of abundance of rain. Ahab went up to eat while Elijah went to the top of Carmel, cast himself down upon the earth, and put his face between his knees to pray.

note.label: 1 Kings 18: The Lord, He Is the God

points: Elijah sent his servant seven times to look toward the sea; at the seventh time he reported a little cloud out of the sea like a man's hand. Elijah sent word to Ahab to prepare his chariot and get down before the rain stopped him, for the hand of the Lord was coming.

note.label: 1 Kings 18: The Lord, He Is the God

points: The heaven grew black with clouds and wind and there was a great rain; Ahab rode to Jezreel, a city in the north in Samaria, and the hand of the Lord was on Elijah so that he girded up his loins and ran before Ahab to the entrance of Jezreel.

note.label: 1 Kings 18: The Lord, He Is the God

points: Ahab told Jezebel all that Elijah had done and how he had slain all the prophets with the sword. This shows the devil on Ahab: he ran back running his mouth about the slain false prophets and never once mentioned that Elijah had brought rain after a three-year drought.

note.label: 1 Kings 19: A Still Small Voice

points: A prophet came unto Ahab saying, Thus saith the Lord, Hast thou seen all this great multitude? I will deliver it into thine hand this day, and thou shalt know that I am the Lord. Asked by whom, the prophet answered, By the young men of the princes of the provinces, and that Ahab himself should order the battle.

note.label: 1 Kings 20: The Lord Is God of the Valleys

points: Naboth had a vineyard next to Ahab's palace in Jezreel, and Ahab asked to trade or buy it, offering a better vineyard or its worth in money.

note.label: 1 Kings 21: Naboth's Vineyard and the Judgment on Ahab

points: Ahab went home heavy and displeased, laid down on his bed, turned away his face, and would eat no bread.

note.label: 1 Kings 21: Naboth's Vineyard and the Judgment on Ahab

points: Jezebel wrote letters in Ahab's name and sealed them with his seal, sending them to the elders and nobles of Naboth's city.
The seal was a signet, an official mark of the king's authority, so the letters carried royal weight as if Ahab himself had written them.

note.label: 1 Kings 21: Naboth's Vineyard and the Judgment on Ahab

points: When Jezebel heard Naboth was dead, she told Ahab to arise and take possession of the vineyard he had been refused.
Ahab shares the guilt. He sat by and let Jezebel commit the crime because he coveted the field, then turned his face from the evil and went to claim the reward.

note.label: 1 Kings 21: Naboth's Vineyard and the Judgment on Ahab

points: Ahab rose up and went down to take the vineyard. This is extortion, seizing what another has by violence and force.

note.label: 1 Kings 21: Naboth's Vineyard and the Judgment on Ahab

points: Ahab called Elijah his enemy, and Elijah answered that he had found him because Ahab had sold himself to work evil in the sight of the Lord.

note.label: 1 Kings 21: Naboth's Vineyard and the Judgment on Ahab

points: Any of Ahab's house dying in the city the dogs would eat, and any dying in the field the fowls of the air would eat, matching the curses spoken in the law.

note.label: 1 Kings 21: Naboth's Vineyard and the Judgment on Ahab

points: There was none like Ahab, who sold himself to work wickedness in the sight of the Lord, stirred up by Jezebel his wife.

note.label: 1 Kings 21: Naboth's Vineyard and the Judgment on Ahab

points: When Ahab heard these words he rent his clothes, put on sackcloth, fasted, and went softly, humbling himself before the Most High.

note.label: 1 Kings 21: Naboth's Vineyard and the Judgment on Ahab

points: Because Ahab humbled himself, the Most High told Elijah he would not bring the evil in Ahab's own days but would bring it upon his house in his son's days.

note.label: 1 Kings 21: Naboth's Vineyard and the Judgment on Ahab

points: The rest of the acts of Ahab, the ivory house he made and the cities he built, are written in the book of the Chronicles of the kings of Israel. Ahab sleeps with his fathers, and Ahaziah his son reigns in his stead.

note.label: 1 Kings 22: A Lying Spirit and the Fall of Ahab

points: Moab rebels against Israel after the death of Ahab. Nations that had been subdued under David and brought under tribute begin to break away, because Israel no longer walks in the blessing that came from serving the Most High.

note.label: 2 Kings 1: Ahaziah Inquires of Beelzebub and Dies

points: Jehoram the son of Ahab begins to reign over Israel in Samaria in the eighteenth year of Jehoshaphat king of Judah and reigns twelve years. He works evil in the sight of the Lord, but not like his father and mother, for he puts away the image of Baal that his father had made.

note.label: 2 Kings 3: Three Kings and the Water in the Ditches

points: Jehoram son of Jehoshaphat begins to reign over Judah and walks in the way of the kings of Israel because the daughter of Ahab was his wife.

note.label: 2 Kings 8: The Prophet Weeps Over Israel's Coming Affliction

points: Ahaziah son of Jehoram begins to reign over Judah and walks in the way of the house of Ahab, being the son-in-law of that house, a picture of the generational curse passed from father to son.

note.label: 2 Kings 8: The Prophet Weeps Over Israel's Coming Affliction

points: Another wicked woman that used the men around her to manipulate the people of Israel: Athaliah. Her son Ahaziah reigned one year in Jerusalem, and he walked in the way of the house of Ahab, and did evil in the sight of the Lord, for he was the son in law of the house of Ahab.

note.label: Are You A Strong Independent Woman?

points: He goes with Jehoram son of Ahab to war against Hazael king of Syria, and the Syrians wound Jehoram at Ramah.

note.label: 2 Kings 8: The Prophet Weeps Over Israel's Coming Affliction

points: The Bible speaks about wicked women and how hard they made it for the nation of Israel. Elisha the prophet sent one of the children of the prophets to Ramoth-gilead to find Jehu, anoint him king over Israel, and then flee. He told him, God sent me to make you the new king, because the original king was wicked: thou shalt smite the house of Ahab thy master, that I may avenge the blood of my servants the prophets at the hand of Jezebel.

note.label: Are You A Strong Independent Woman?

points: Jehu is charged to smite the house of Ahab to avenge the blood of the prophets and of the servants of the Most High shed at the hand of Jezebel, whose work was to kill the prophets while weak Ahab let it continue.

note.label: 2 Kings 9: Jehu Anointed and the Wicked Kings Cut Off

points: Jehu writes to the rulers of Jezreel who kept Ahab's seventy sons, challenging them to set up a son and fight, but they are exceedingly afraid because two kings could not stand before him.

note.label: 2 Kings 10: Jehu Destroys Baal and Falls Short of the Law

points: The heads are laid in two heaps at the gate, and Jehu slays all that remained of the house of Ahab, his great men, kinsfolk, and priests, until none remained, according to the word spoken by Elijah.

note.label: 2 Kings 10: Jehu Destroys Baal and Falls Short of the Law

points: At Samaria Jehu slays all that remained unto Ahab, destroying him according to the saying of the Most High spoken to Elijah.

note.label: 2 Kings 10: Jehu Destroys Baal and Falls Short of the Law

points: The Most High commends Jehu for executing what is right against the house of Ahab and promises his children to the fourth generation shall sit on the throne of Israel.

note.label: 2 Kings 10: Jehu Destroys Baal and Falls Short of the Law

points: Manasseh began at twelve and reigned fifty-five years, and did not follow his father's example: he rebuilt the high places Hezekiah had cast down, reared altars to Baal and a grove as Ahab did, and worshipped the host of heaven, the stars and the zodiac.

note.label: The Mercy and Humility of King Manasseh

points: He rebuilds the high places Hezekiah destroyed, rears altars for Baal, makes a grove as Ahab did, and worships the host of heaven, even building altars in the house of the Most High where He set His name; this is a wickedness with zero fear of the Most High.

note.label: 2 Kings 21: The Wickedness of Manasseh and Amon

points: He will stretch over Jerusalem the line of Samaria and the plummet of the house of Ahab, and wipe Jerusalem as a man wipes a dish and turns it upside down; the same desolation done to Samaria will reach Judah.

note.label: 2 Kings 21: The Wickedness of Manasseh and Amon

points: Jehoshaphat had riches and honor and abundance, and joined affinity with Ahab through marriage.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 18: Jehoshaphat, Ahab, and the True Prophet

points: Ahab feasted him and persuaded him to go up to Ramoth Gilead, and Jehoshaphat answered, I am as thou art, my people as thy people, we will be with thee in the war.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 18: Jehoshaphat, Ahab, and the True Prophet

points: He walked in the way of the kings of Israel, as did the house of Ahab, meaning he was wicked; Israel's kings were all wicked, and he had the daughter of Ahab to wife.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 21: Jehoram's Wicked Reign

points: Elijah charged him with making Judah and Jerusalem go a whoring like the whoredoms of the house of Ahab, and with slaying his brethren who were better than himself.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 21: Jehoram's Wicked Reign

points: He also walked in the ways of the house of Ahab: for his mother was his counsellor to do wickedly. That is the same thing that mother was explaining with her daughters and her sons. Sons got to do whatever and be whatever. And they did not have any real guidance, because the mother did not know how. But she was raising her daughters to be so-called better than her, tough and independent. And she noticed that she was creating a bigger problem, because now they have got a mindset that they do not need a man.

note.label: From Broken Men Comes Ungodly Generations

points: He walked in the ways of the house of Ahab, for his mother was his counsellor to do wickedly, and the house of Ahab were his counsellors after his father died, to his destruction.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 22: Ahaziah and the Rise of Athaliah

points: Wherefore he did evil in the sight of the Lord like the house of Ahab: for they were his counsellers after the death of his father to his destruction. And that is where we are at with society. We have taught our kids that they are nothing.

note.label: From Broken Men Comes Ungodly Generations

points: Ahaziah walked after their counsel and went with Jehoram son of Ahab to war against Hazael king of Syria at Ramoth-gilead, where Jehoram was wounded.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 22: Ahaziah and the Rise of Athaliah

points: He went down to see the wounded Jehoram at Jezreel, and the destruction of Ahaziah was of the Most High, for by going he came into the path of Jehu, whom the Most High had anointed to cut off the house of Ahab.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 22: Ahaziah and the Rise of Athaliah

points: That same Jehu who killed the seventy sons of Ahab found the princes of Judah and the sons of Ahaziah's brethren and slew them, then sought and caught Ahaziah, who was hid in Samaria.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 22: Ahaziah and the Rise of Athaliah

points: For the statutes of Omri are kept, and all the works of the house of Ahab, and ye walk in their counsels; therefore ye shall bear the reproach of my people.

note.label: Micah 6: What Doth the Lord Require of Thee
